# Tanya's Sprint Retro

Tanya: "We shipped the async decision widget. Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter. The Zephyr integration was the key unlock."

segments.exact: We shipped the async decision widget.
Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter.
The Zephyr integration was the key unlock.

observations.why: An integration spoken of AS a lock mechanism ('unlock') — a thing functioning as another thing, not mere vividness.
Native pipeline jargon ('unlock' as a shipped-enabler noun) marks a technical register shift from the plain-spoken baseline of the other two segments.
Completed action in the past naming a specific artifact (the async decision widget).
Reports a settled, specific past measurement with a concrete numeric value.
Past-tense attribution of causal significance to a named, specific integration.

evidence.quote: We shipped the async decision widget.

observations.why: Straightforward declarative of a completed accomplishment; settled satisfaction, no energized markers.
Superlative registers quiet pride in the result, but the register stays informational rather than energized.
Positive evaluation of an enabler, delivered in a measured retrospective register without arousal markers.

evidence.quote: We shipped the async decision widget.

observations.why: Speaker controls the factual record of what was delivered, supplying the fact itself as a completed accomplishment.

evidence.quote: Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter.

observations.why: Citing a measured metric with a superlative frames the fact as evidence supporting an implicit claim of strong performance.

evidence.quote: The Zephyr integration was the key unlock.

observations.why: Speaker supplies and frames a causal fact, controlling which factor is named as the decisive one.

evidence.quote: We shipped the async decision widget.

observations.why: Past-tense performed declarative recording a completed ship — ratification of a settled, load-bearing outcome.

evidence.quote: Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter.

observations.why: Unhedged factual assertion ready to defend, but no ratification language or operational rule — claim, not decision.

evidence.quote: The Zephyr integration was the key unlock.

observations.why: Committed evaluative assertion with no hedge, but argued-for rather than ratified — claim level.
Shipping is the craft-completion act; the sentence performs delivery as achievement of capability.
Superlative framing appeals to achievement and standing — velocity as a competitive benchmark.
Naming an integration as the 'key unlock' frames capability mastery — the tool that enabled the outcome.
The 'we' pronoun enacts communal-sharing, pooling the team into one body that shipped together.
Quantifying output in points enacts market-pricing proportionality — performance measured by a numeric metric.

payload.rationale: The document is a sprint retro by Tanya covering three load-bearing concepts: (1) the async decision widget shipping — which connects to the existing Sprint 4 retro sample, the thesis-proven position, and the anti-Slack positioning narrative; (2) velocity at 23 points — which connects to the velocity observation and the metric-anchoring style observation; (3) Zephyr integration as key unlock — which connects directly to the Zephyr integration position. I expanded the anti-Slack narrative's children (anti-pattern real-time chat, pricing, product category, target market) because the widget shipping is evidence that bears on the core positioning thesis and the pricing evolution ($12 → $15). The style observations are included so the passes can recognize the direct-quote and metric-anchoring patterns this document follows. I did not expand further into packaging or segmentation subtrees since this retro does not introduce new pricing or segmentation decisions.
